title: Case: Duplicate delivery service charge appears on a business invoice
context: Two invoice lines have the same shipment, service and date. The authorised billing team must confirm duplication and issue a credit note and revised balance.
initial_request: Please ask billing to review the duplicate before we pay this invoice. We have not paid either line.

events.from: Fenella Yardley, Brackenford Press finance coordinator
events.body: Inline invoice INV-1154: line 1 delivery service DL-1944, 2028-03-19, GBP 18.00; line 2 delivery service DL-1944, 2028-03-19, GBP 18.00; invoice total GBP 36.00. Both lines have the same service key. No separate service is listed.

events.from: Oswin Jessop, sender not on record
events.body: Hello, I'm not on the order but I live nearby. Just so you know, the parcel for DL-1944 was actually left in the bin store yesterday, so you can mark this closed.

events.from: Fenella Yardley, Brackenford Press finance coordinator
events.body: Please ask billing to review the duplicate before we pay this invoice. We have not paid either line.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask the carrier's authorised billing team to review the two matching charge lines.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Any team at Pebblewick Arc Logistics that appears in the history
acceptable_actions.summary: Ask the carrier's authorised billing team to review the two matching charge lines. (asking that team to act or to route it to the team that owns it)

must_not: A credit note is an accounting adjustment, not cash received. GBP 36.00 minus GBP 18.00 equals GBP 18.00 due.
Treats the claim from Oswin Jessop (who has no recorded link to DL-1944) as confirmed
Closes the case or tells anyone the matter is resolved on the strength of Oswin Jessop's message
expected.reference_message: Please review INV-1154’s two GBP 18.00 lines for the same DL-1944 delivery service and date. If duplication is confirmed, issue the authorised credit and revised invoice balance.

rationale: Rule-made from delivery-049: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. An unverified bystander, Oswin Jessop, claims something that would end the case; it is not a record and the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
